claims.claim: This period's RLHF-adjacent work is less about new preference objectives than about how to make model behavior legible, controllable, and cheaper to supervise.
claims.issue: No offered abstract says anything about making supervision cheaper; 'controllable' is also not shown. Framing invented.

claims.claim: Counterfactual self-explanations become more faithful and decision-relevant as model scale increases.
claims.span: larger models are substantially more likely to generate counterfactuals that flip their own predictions and target decision-relevant evidence

claims.claim: Rationale-guided prompting makes edits more minimal and human-aligned but does not reliably improve faithfulness.
claims.span: the rationale-guided condition produces edit-minimal counterfactuals that are also more human-aligned. However, it does not consistently improve faithfulness
claims.issue: Minor: the abstract says 'rationale-guided condition'; that it is prompting is not stated.

claims.claim: A paired counterfactual benchmark can separate unsupported answering, conflict blindness, and wrong non-answer actions.
claims.span: EviScope therefore distinguishes unsupported answering, conflict blindness, and wrong non-answer actions

claims.claim: On local models, an explicit evidence-action gate underperforms vanilla RAG on QCS.
claims.span: On two local open models, an explicit evidence-action gate underperforms vanilla RAG on QCS: 0.15 vs. 0.50 for Qwen and 0.10 vs. 0.375 for Llama
claims.issue: 'QCS' is never defined for the reader.

claims.claim: Gemini still answers 5% of contradiction cases.
claims.span: yet still answers 5% of conflict cases after contradiction insertion

claims.claim: A third line pushes supervision into retrieval and memory.
claims.issue: RELEX gives example recipes to human learners; it is not model supervision. Grouping it with ICML as a 'line' of supervision work is an invented thread.

claims.claim: Personalized example retrieval improves procedural writing.
claims.span: Our results show that providing tailored examples contributes to better writing performance and user experience.

claims.claim: Interactive memory learning uses online RL to improve long-term conversation quality as interactions accumulate.
claims.span: ICML utilizes an online reinforcement learning mechanism ... exhibiting the unique capability to continuously improve response quality as interactions accumulate

claims.claim: Pick hook: quantifies faithfulness, minimality, and rationale alignment across ten LLaMA-3 and Qwen-2.5 models, and shows scale matters more than the prompting trick.
claims.span: we evaluate ten instruction-tuned models from the LLaMA-3 and Qwen-2.5 families, measuring faithfulness, minimality, and alignment with human-annotated rationales. Our results show that model scale is the strongest determinant of explanation quality

overviews.pick_note: 2609.17119 is in pool; the reasonable pick (rest of pool is mostly off-topic math/robotics plus RELEX).
overviews.note: Two invented framings: 'cheaper to supervise' and 'pushes supervision into retrieval and memory' (RELEX is for human learners). Cited claims are accurate. 125 words, QCS undefined.

claims.claim: This period's PINN work pushed hardest on making physics constraints usable in harder, more structured settings: regional power-system dispatch, inverse transport inference, and multi-output surrogates.
claims.issue: 'Pushed hardest' ranks the week's emphasis; the offered set is dominated by training/method papers (conflict-free gradients, AD vs discretization, Gauss-Newton, debiased PINNs, hypernetworks), so the claimed main thrust is not shown by the set.

claims.claim: A progressive latent-bottleneck PINN encodes differential frequency nadir and support integrals inside a CVaR day-ahead dispatch model.
claims.span: a progressive latent-bottleneck physics-informed neural network is applied to characterize differential frequency nadir terms and regional frequency support integral terms ... a day ahead dispatch model is developed in which regional stochastic frequency constraints are embedded using a CVaR-based formulation

claims.claim: Improving regional nadir and RoCoF by 32.76% and 2.06% on IEEE 118-bus.
claims.span: A case study on the IEEE 118-bus system ... with the regional frequency nadir and RoCoF improved by 32.76% and 2.06%, respectively.

claims.claim: An inverse PINN recovered a conductivity law with under-10% error in the data-constrained region.
claims.span: The framework is first validated using synthetic data generated from a prescribed conductivity function ... The model recovers the imposed functional dependence with errors below 10 % in the data-constrained region.
claims.issue: Drops the setting: the <10% figure is on synthetic data with a prescribed ground truth; the experimental TJ-II run is only 'an initial estimate'.

claims.claim: Bootstrap resampling flags reliability.
claims.span: Bootstrap resampling is shown to provide a practical indicator of prediction reliability and consistency.

claims.claim: A Martian thermosphere model reduced non-physical density inversions while preserving or slightly improving RMSE/MAE/R2.
claims.span: physics-informed regularization substantially reduces non-physical inversions while preserving predictive skill and slightly improving it in the best-performing configuration, as measured by RMSE, MAE, and R^2

claims.claim: A GRB gap-reconstruction study found stronger uncertainty reduction from a broken-power-law PINN prior but at a higher outlier rate than data-driven baselines.
claims.span: The PINN broken power-law prior achieves the largest reductions (~41--49%) at a higher outlier rate (~15--20%), while ReFANN, the Siamese network, and PQR deliver consistent reductions (~19--27%) with outlier fractions (<~4%)

claims.claim: Pick hook: benchmarks a PINN against three non-PINN reconstructions on 545 GRBs and quantifies the tradeoff between 41-49% uncertainty reduction and a 15-20% outlier rate.
claims.span: this work benchmarks four models on 545 Swift-XRT GRBs ... The PINN broken power-law prior achieves the largest reductions (~41--49%) at a higher outlier rate (~15--20%)

overviews.note: 'pushed hardest' ranking not shown by the set (error); '<10% error' cited to 2609.11628 drops that it is on synthetic data. Otherwise precise. 136 words, over target.

claims.claim: This period's PINN work split between harder physics targets and sharper training/representation tricks.
claims.span: Neutral framing of the five cited papers (boson star Q-ball, Cu-Zr glasses; tree embeddings, ARRB, periodic activation).

claims.claim: PINNs were used as a proof of concept for a rotating Q-ball inside a broader boson-star benchmark effort.
claims.span: As a further proof of concept, we also present the use of physics-informed neural networks to construct a rotating Q-ball solution.

claims.claim: A multi-task PINN on Cu-Zr metallic glasses predicted temperature with 23.4 K MAE and classified liquid/supercooled/glass states at 96.6% accuracy.
claims.span: The classification task achieves 96.6% test accuracy ... the regression head yields a mean absolute error of 23.4 K on a trajectory-disjoint held-out test set.

claims.claim: Autograd constraints improved adherence to motif-temperature trends.
claims.span: physics constraints can be incorporated over a broad range of loss weights without compromising predictive accuracy, while substantially improving compliance with the prescribed physical trends

claims.claim: Tree positional embeddings improved symbolic ODE transformers across data sizes.
claims.span: tree positional embeddings aid learning in early epochs and continue to improve performance throughout, ultimately yielding consistent advantages across various data sizes and tasks

claims.claim: Contrastive learning (also) improved symbolic ODE transformers across data sizes.
claims.span: we apply contrastive learning to support the commutative property in mathematics
claims.issue: The abstract reports no performance gain from contrastive learning; the 'across data sizes' result is for tree positional embeddings only.

claims.claim: Hard boundary embedding plus adaptive regional residual balancing drove Falkner-Skan errors down to 6.691e-7 in wall shear with residual MSE 6.357e-9.
claims.span: For (β0,β1)=(0.75,0.50), the predicted wall shear ... giving an absolute error of 6.691e-7. The residual MSE is 6.357e-9
claims.issue: Numbers are for one (β0,β1) case and a single seed ('multi-seed experiments remain necessary'); presented as the Falkner-Skan result in general.

claims.claim: Periodic activations helped sparse-flow reconstruction, cutting cost for comparable quality.
claims.span: the improved architecture enables reaching similar reconstruction qualities for a fraction of the expense
claims.issue: Minor blur: the gain is from the sine+cosine (complex exponential) activation over sine-activated MLPs, not periodic activations per se.

claims.claim: Pick hook: exact boundary admissibility, regional residual balancing, and deterministic checkpointing deliver sub-micro error on Falkner-Skan with ablations showing where the gain comes from.
claims.span: A matched single-seed ablation shows that ARRB reduces residual MSE by 52.81% ... the relative L2 errors in f' and f'' are 2.848e-6 and 4.188e-5
claims.issue: 'Sub-micro error' holds only for wall-shear absolute error in one case (f'' relative L2 is 4e-5); the only ablation is single-seed and of ARRB, so it does not show a gain from checkpointing.

claims.claim: Pick hook: multi-task interpretable PINN coupling regression and phase classification, reports uncertainty checks, shows physics constraints can be weighted broadly without hurting accuracy.
claims.span: Five-fold trajectory-grouped cross-validation, deep-ensemble predictions, and Monte Carlo dropout are used to assess model robustness and predictive uncertainty. Sensitivity analyses demonstrate that physics constraints can be incorporated over a broad range of loss weights without compromising predictive accuracy

overviews.pick_note: Both picks in pool and reasonable.
overviews.note: Contrastive learning credited with gains the abstract never reports (error). Falkner-Skan numbers are one case, one seed; pick hook 'sub-micro error ... ablations showing where the gain comes from' overstates.

claims.claim: This period's PINN work pushed into settings where the physics prior is not just a residual but a structural constraint on the representation or inference target.
claims.issue: Doesn't fit 2 of the 3 papers it introduces: the unlearning paper uses exactly the physics residual ('The physics residual acts as a safety fence'), and HJSO is an optimizer. Even in the pion paper most constraints 'enter through the loss functional'.

claims.claim: A conformal PINN for the pion form factor enforced charge normalization, Schwarz reflection, analyticity, dispersion relations, Watson's theorem, and pQCD asymptotics in a z-plane map.
claims.span: charge normalisation and Schwarz reflection are enforced by construction, while Cauchy-Riemann analyticity, dispersion relations, Watson's theorem, and perturbative QCD asymptotics enter through the loss functional
claims.issue: Blurs hard vs soft (loss) constraints; acceptable PINN usage of 'enforced'.

claims.claim: Model-independent charge radius of 0.435 ± 0.008(stat) ± 0.007(cali) fm^2 and pole parameters for the ρ resonance.
claims.span: We obtain model-independent estimates of the pion charge radius, <r_π^2> = 0.435 ± 0.008_stat ± 0.007_cali fm^2, the second-sheet pole parameters

claims.claim: Reduced-space Levenberg-Marquardt refinement sped up parameter-of-interest recovery in an inverse Bratu PINN.
claims.span: an inverse Bratu problem solved with a physics-informed neural network ... HJSO reaches prescribed POI-error thresholds faster than the corresponding joint first-order baseline

claims.claim: A physics-guided unlearning scheme used residuals as a safety fence to remove poison and restore compliance in distribution-grid controllers.
claims.span: The physics residual acts as a safety fence during gradient ascent ... our proposed physics-guided model simultaneously removes poison and restores physical compliance

claims.claim: Pick hook: shows how far PINNs can be pushed when analyticity, dispersion, and asymptotics are built into the network rather than fitted afterward.
claims.span: Cauchy-Riemann analyticity, dispersion relations, Watson's theorem, and perturbative QCD asymptotics enter through the loss functional
claims.issue: Those three are soft loss terms, not built into the network; only normalisation and Schwarz reflection are 'enforced by construction'.

claims.claim: Pick hook: isolates low-dimensional parameters of interest and refines them with reduced-space LM inside a PINN inverse problem.
claims.span: freeze the remaining variables while applying a reduced-space Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) refinement to the POIs ... an inverse Bratu problem solved with a physics-informed neural network

overviews.pick_note: Both in pool; good choices (pool also has an insurance platform paper).
overviews.note: Lead 'not just a residual but a structural constraint' contradicts the unlearning paper ('The physics residual acts as a safety fence') (error). Pick hook 'built into the network' overstates: analyticity/dispersion/asymptotics 'enter through the loss functional'.

claims.claim: This period's PINN work concentrated on making the physics prior structurally harder to violate, either by changing the training schedule or by embedding the right operator geometry into the model.
claims.issue: SoftServe is a general deep-learning optimizer, not a way to make a physics prior harder to violate; 'concentrated' ranks a week whose 24 papers cover many other things (NTK positivity, Bayesian PINN collider bias, sampling, KANs).

claims.claim: Causality-enforced evolutional networks split time into nonoverlapping subintervals, trained sequentially from the initial step.
claims.span: we divide the time domain into nonoverlapping subintervals, assign a unique neural network to each subinterval ... The proposed networks undergo sequential training, beginning with the initial time step.

claims.claim: Reported better accuracy with less memory and compute than standard PINNs on several problems.
claims.span: significant improvement in accuracy for long-time simulations of various PDE problems where the original PINN method fails while it requires less computational cost and memory compared to the PINN method

claims.claim: SoftServe extends quasi-Newton updates to PINNs with positive-definite curvature estimates and GPU-friendly Newton-Schulz iterations.
claims.span: SoftServe derives positivedefinite curvature estimates ... relies on the stable coupled Newton-Schulz iteration ... replacing costly matrix decompositions with GPU-friendly matrix multiplications
claims.issue: Scope blur: it is a general deep-learning QN method; PINNs are one test task.

claims.claim: It is reported to beat Adam, Muon, and SOAP on ill-conditioned tasks including a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model.
claims.span: often achieving lower losses than established baselines including Adam, Muon, and SOAP
claims.issue: 'beat' drops the abstract's hedge 'often'.

claims.claim: Conformal and multiphysics formulations kept pushing accuracy by enforcing the right constraints, from exact symmetries to temperature-dependent properties.
claims.span: Under hard boundary constraints, QPINNs using exact symmetrization and randomized encoding achieve the lowest mean errors in the two benchmarks, respectively. / MCoPINN ... reconstructing temperature-dependent thermophysical properties from sparse material data
claims.issue: Neither paper is 'conformal'; 2610.01874 is a quantum ML symmetrization paper (QPINNs), which the sentence hides. MCoPINN reconstructs temperature-dependent properties rather than enforcing them as constraints.

claims.claim: Pick hook: attacks the core PINN failure mode by enforcing temporal causality through subinterval networks and sequential training, with explicit claims of lower memory and better accuracy.
claims.span: their applicability in the long-time integration of partial differential equations (PDEs) remains constrained. We argue that this problem stems from the lack of consideration of temporal causality
claims.issue: The abstract is about the long-time-integration failure, not 'the core PINN failure mode'.

claims.claim: Pick hook: scalable quasi-Newton recipe with positive-definite curvature estimates; reports gains on PINNs and a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model.
claims.span: SoftServe excels on problems that are severely ill-conditioned, including ... physics-informed neural networks, and a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model, often achieving lower losses

overviews.note: Invented lead thread; 'conformal ... formulations' fits neither cited paper and hides that 2610.01874 is quantum ML. 'beat Adam, Muon, and SOAP' drops 'often'; pick calls long-time integration 'the core PINN failure mode'.

claims.claim: This period's PINN work split between harder structural priors and more explicit uncertainty or conditioning.
claims.span: Loose framing of the two papers covered (holographic reconstruction priors; stochastic PINN for UQ).
claims.issue: 'conditioning' is vague.

claims.claim: A PINN reconstructed black-brane geometries and scalar potentials from thermodynamics, UV asymptotics, Ward identities, and horizon regularity.
claims.span: We then reconstruct nonlinear black-brane geometries and the scalar potential using thermodynamics, ultraviolet asymptotics, Ward identities, and horizon regularity.

claims.claim: The authors show that matching the equation of state alone does not fix the bulk potential.
claims.span: accurately reproducing thermodynamics with a trained PINN does not guarantee an accurate reconstruction of the scalar potential

claims.claim: Pinning the cubic coupling to its exact value cut the maximum sampled self-interaction error by about 15x.
claims.span: Fixing the cubic coupling to its exact PW value ... reduces the maximum sampled error in the reconstructed scalar self-interactions by a factor of ~15 compared with constraining only the bulk scalar mass

claims.claim: Adding bulk-viscosity information cut it by another 13x while reproducing viscosity within 0.09%.
claims.span: Adding knowledge of the bulk viscosity ... further reduces this error by an additional factor of ~13, with independent forward solutions reproducing the bulk viscosity within 0.09%

claims.claim: A manifold-based SPINN couples a common Gaussian germ to both random operators and random neuron locations.
claims.span: a common Gaussian stochastic germ drives both the SBVP random operator and a manifold-based stochastic neural architecture ... generate random neuron locations
claims.issue: Second pass: the abstract says the germ drives the operator and 'a manifold-based stochastic neural architecture', but neuron locations come from 'a latent Gaussian field and an inhomogeneous Poisson point process'. It never says the germ drives the neuron locations, so that specific coupling isn't supported.

claims.claim: Training on observation-space likelihoods plus distribution alignment.
claims.span: Training is performed in observation space ... combines data fidelity, through negative log-likelihood, with a cross-entropy alignment term

claims.claim: Models non-Gaussian random operators with reduced-variance gradients.
claims.span: can represent non-Gaussian random operators ... The shared stochastic germ yields common-random-numbers Monte Carlo estimators and reduced-variance gradients.

claims.claim: Pick hook: quantifies when thermodynamics alone leaves the bulk potential underdetermined, and how much exact coupling and viscosity information tighten the reconstruction.
claims.span: does not guarantee an accurate reconstruction of the scalar potential ... by a factor of ~15 ... an additional factor of ~13

claims.claim: Pick hook: turns the physics prior into a shared random germ and a manifold-based random architecture, with a likelihood-plus-alignment objective for random-operator learning.
claims.span: The method enforces physics through a structural probabilistic coupling: a common Gaussian stochastic germ drives both the SBVP random operator and a manifold-based stochastic neural architecture.

overviews.pick_note: Both in pool; picks just repeat the two papers the overview covers.
overviews.note: Changed on second pass: 'couples a common Gaussian germ to both random operators and random neuron locations' says more than the abstract, which ties neuron locations to 'a latent Gaussian field and an inhomogeneous Poisson point process'. Holography part is exact.
overviews.second_pass: Re-checked: EoS-alone claim (holds), 15x/13x figures (hold), germ-to-neuron-location coupling (changed to overstated).

claims.claim: This period's PINN work is split between failure modes and domain-specific fixes.
claims.span: Neutral framing of the HJI failure-mode paper and the seismology/magnetics/KAN application papers.

claims.claim: For HJI problems, residual minimization can drive the residual near zero while converging to folded almost-everywhere solutions with values wrong over most of the domain.
claims.span: converges to folded almost-everywhere solutions in all 30 runs: small residuals and the expected capture-layer gradient, yet values that are wrong over most of the domain

claims.claim: On a pursuit-evasion benchmark, a standard Fourier-feature network failed in all 30 runs.
claims.span: A standard network with periodic Fourier features converges to folded almost-everywhere solutions in all 30 runs

claims.claim: Feeding geodesic distance recovered the viscosity solution in all 30 runs, and a chart-based periodic model succeeded in 27 of 30.
claims.span: a single network fed the wrapped displacement and its distance recovers the viscosity solution in all 30 runs, while a minimum over periodic image charts succeeds in 27 of 30

claims.claim: Extending travel-time PINNs from P to P and S waves required redesigning collocation, architecture, and optimization because S-wave gradients were steeper.
claims.span: considerably steeper travel-time gradients, the original PINN training procedure ... was insufficient. We therefore revised the training procedure by reconsidering the distribution of collocation points, the NN architecture, and the optimizer.

claims.claim: The revised system reduced RMS deviations against fast marching and worked on 223 earthquakes.
claims.span: substantially reduced the root-mean-square deviations for both P- and S-waves compared with the original algorithm ... When applied to 223 earthquakes ... yielded hypocenters generally consistent with the JMA catalog beneath the network

claims.claim: Other papers pushed PINNs into magnetic-field reconstruction from Maxwell constraints.
claims.span: a physics-informed neural network (PINN) method which reconstructs three-dimensional magnetic fields subject to the source-free Maxwell equations

claims.claim: Time-fractional Navier-Stokes on complex domains with a geometry-gated, divergence-free KAN that outperformed PINN baselines.
claims.span: GeoDiv KAN achieves higher predictive accuracy than PINN, PIKAN, RBF KAN, and DF RBFKAN across the considered benchmark problems

claims.claim: ... and outperformed CFD reconstructions.
claims.span: GeoDiv KAN is applied to two data driven CFD cases
claims.issue: The abstract only says it was applied to two CFD datasets; no comparison against CFD is reported.

claims.claim: Pick hook: shows a concrete PINN pathology (tiny residuals, wrong viscosity solution) and tests three parameterizations, including one that succeeds in all 30 runs.
claims.span: We train four neural parameterizations with ten seeds on each geometry, 120 runs in total.
claims.issue: Wrong count: four parameterizations, not three.

claims.claim: Pick hook: adds S-wave support, explains why the old training failed, and reports improved RMS errors plus 223-event application results.
claims.span: extends the framework to both P- and S-wave travel times ... Because the resulting S-wave velocity structure has ... considerably steeper travel-time gradients, the original PINN training procedure ... was insufficient

overviews.pick_note: Both in pool; strongest two in the pool.
overviews.note: 'outperformed PINN baselines and CFD reconstructions': no CFD comparison in the abstract. Pick says 'tests three parameterizations'; the abstract says four. Strong concrete content, but 144 words.

claims.claim: This period's PINN papers pushed hardest on regimes with sharp gradients, discontinuities, or inverse identification.
claims.issue: Ranks the week's emphasis without support; of 15 offered papers many are about failure modes, symmetry/NTK, sampling and conflict-free gradients; the turbulence paper it then cites is about neither discontinuities nor inverse identification.

claims.claim: A PINN handled an abrupt PN junction in one and two dimensions, with extreme carrier gradients and a discontinuous doping profile.
claims.span: an abrupt PN-junction in both one and two dimensions that features extreme gradients of the carrier concentrations at the Ohmic contacts and an abrupt discontinuity in the doping profile

claims.claim: It matched commercial TCAD accuracy across all observables and bias conditions.
claims.span: with errors comparable to traditional simulation software ... we are able to retrieve accurate results for all observables under all bias conditions
claims.issue: Fuses two separate statements into a stronger one; the comparator is 'traditional simulation software', not explicitly commercial TCAD, and 'comparable' becomes 'matched'.

claims.claim: While also tackling doping retrieval.
claims.span: we apply the PINN solver towards the inverse problem of retrieving doping profiles

claims.claim: A KdVB-PINN paired forward solving with sensitivity analysis over eight parameters.
claims.span: a sensitivity analysis is introduced that quantifies ... how each of eight physical parameters influences the KdVB equation

claims.claim: Seven single-parameter inversions gave 0.8-2.1% errors for five parameters, one converged only partially, and surface tension was unidentifiable.
claims.span: single-parameter inverse estimation is performed for seven of the eight parameters ... estimated with errors of 0.8-2.1%, the polytropic exponent converges only partially, and the surface tension coefficient cannot be estimated at all

claims.claim: PINNs tracked 2D/3D turbulent molecular clouds over multiple free-fall times.
claims.span: PINNs accurately recover the global evolution of the flow over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities

claims.claim: Training cost rising by less than 25% from 128^3 to 1024^3.
claims.span: increasing by less than 25% from 128^3 to 1024^3 in our experiments

claims.claim: Pick hook: a hard-constrained solver coping with abrupt junctions, extreme carrier gradients, and inverse doping recovery under all bias conditions.
claims.span: using advanced training techniques ... retrieving doping profiles directly from desired electric field distributions or electrostatic potentials under non-zero applied biases
claims.issue: Nothing says the solver is hard-constrained; 'all bias conditions' belongs to the forward results, the inverse problem is only 'under non-zero applied biases'.

claims.claim: Pick hook: combines a PINN with parameter sensitivity ranking and shows which parameters can be estimated to 0.8-2.1% and which cannot be identified.
claims.span: allowing the expected difficulty of estimating each parameter to be assessed in advance ... the surface tension coefficient cannot be estimated at all

overviews.note: Unsupported 'pushed hardest' lead. 2610.33133: 'matched commercial TCAD accuracy' inflates 'comparable to traditional simulation software'; pick invents 'hard-constrained' and moves 'all bias conditions' onto the inverse problem.

claims.claim: This period's PINN work pushed into harder inverse and nonlinear regimes while tightening numerical guarantees.
claims.span: Loose framing of the four cited papers (e15 inverse identification, nonlinear water waves, NS; interval certification).
claims.issue: The Love-number paper is a forward problem, so 'inverse' covers only one paper.

claims.claim: A PINN with exact horizon conditions and an H2-Sobolev residual loss recovered scalar, vector, and tensor Love numbers with relative errors below 10^-5.
claims.span: Across the tested scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations, the method recovers the finite dissipative response with relative errors below 10^-5 ... The conservative response, which vanishes analytically, is constrained by the numerical error floor.
claims.issue: The <1e-5 figure is for the dissipative response only, not the Love numbers as a whole.

claims.claim: Higher-derivative terms improved accuracy by orders of magnitude.
claims.span: Controlled comparisons show that the higher-derivative loss terms improve solution accuracy by orders of magnitude

claims.claim: PINNs were used as a search engine for periodic gravity-capillary traveling waves, reaching near-machine-precision residuals.
claims.span: Physics-informed neural networks are used as a search mechanism ... the neural networks achieve near-machine-precision residuals of the governing equations

claims.claim: Enabling rigorous interval-arithmetic certification plus Lean formalization of a candidate solution.
claims.span: We freeze one candidate ... and rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic ... We formalize the certification argument in Lean

claims.claim: Exact boundary/initial embeddings cut e15 identification errors to 0.15%-0.51%.
claims.span: In a six-way comparison (plane-strain PZT-5H, manufactured wavefield, 30 dB noise) ... The constrained formulations reach mean e15 errors between 0.15% and 0.51% ... On finite-element data ... recovers e15 with 1.19% mean error
claims.issue: Best-case range from the manufactured-wavefield test presented without its setting; on finite-element data the error is 1.19% (0.65-2.71% across noise).

claims.claim: A projection-style segregated PINN improved incompressible Navier-Stokes convergence by decoupling momentum and pressure.
claims.span: the nonlinear NS equations are decoupled into the linearized momentum and pressure Poisson equations ... The improved convergence and accuracy are demonstrated

claims.claim: Pick hook: near-machine-precision nonlinear wave solving, then independently bounds the residual with interval arithmetic and formalizes the proof in Lean.
claims.span: rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic ... This independently validates the neural-network accuracy. We formalize the certification argument in Lean

claims.claim: Pick hook: exact horizon enforcement plus an H2-Sobolev loss gets Love numbers to below 10^-5 relative error and isolates solver error from response-extraction error.
claims.span: recovers the finite dissipative response with relative errors below 10^-5 ... independent tests of the extraction procedure distinguish solver errors from errors in recovering the response coefficients
claims.issue: Same generalization: the 1e-5 figure is the dissipative response only.

overviews.pick_note: Both in pool and the strongest two; 2611.03485 and 2611.07387 are cited in the overview but are not in the pick pool (allowed).
overviews.note: Concrete and mostly faithful, but 'Love numbers with relative errors below 10^-5' (overview and pick) is only the 'finite dissipative response'; e15 '0.15%-0.51%' is the manufactured-data best case (FE data: 1.19%).

claims.claim: This period splits between making PINNs more trustworthy as a research tool and making them more faithful to PDE structure.
claims.span: Framing of the two cited papers (evaluation protocol; well-balanced WE-PINN).

claims.claim: PINNeval argues that many benchmark claims are fragile because they isolate one pipeline component while freezing the rest at noncompetitive defaults.
claims.span: many existing benchmarks study these components in isolation ... set the surrounding and not considered components of the pipeline to a minimal default that is no longer representative of current best practice approaches. Conclusions drawn under such conditions may not transfer to competitive pipelines.

claims.claim: It evaluates domain-importance adaptation, loss balancing, architecture, and optimization as an integrated system.
claims.span: a new evaluation protocol that (1) treats the four components as an integrated system

claims.claim: Ships PINNpipe with 18 methods and nine benchmark problems.
claims.span: we release PINNpipe, an innovative JAX package containing 18 different methods from the current literature as well as nine efficiently implemented benchmark problems

claims.claim: A weak/entropy PINN is extended to shallow water with smooth and discontinuous bathymetry, using randomly placed overlapping control volumes, exact bed-slope correction, and subdomain coupling.
claims.span: enforced on randomly placed control volumes that may overlap ... a cell-local bed-slope correction makes the quadrature reproduce the exact bed increment. Bed discontinuities ... separate sub-domains carrying independent networks, coupled through conservation of discharge and total head

claims.claim: So the lake-at-rest residual vanishes to round-off and is an exact global minimizer.
claims.span: We prove that the fully discrete residual vanishes identically on the lake at rest ... so that the equilibrium is an exact global minimiser of the training objective ... Numerically, the residual vanishes to round-off

claims.claim: Pick hook: formalizes what a fair PINN benchmark should hold fixed, what must be competitive, and provides PINNpipe with 18 methods and nine problems.
claims.span: crucially requires competitive implementations of the components not under investigation; (3) specifies the metrics and reporting format

claims.claim: Pick hook: proves exact lake-at-rest minimization over smooth and discontinuous bathymetry and shows how weak residuals, bed corrections, and subdomain coupling fit together.
claims.span: We prove that the fully discrete residual vanishes identically on the lake at rest for any control-volume family ... so that the equilibrium is an exact global minimiser

overviews.pick_note: Both in pool and the strongest two.
overviews.note: All claims trace to the abstracts. Covers only 2 of 19 papers; the PINNeval sentence says nothing about what its results found.
overviews.second_pass: Re-checked: 'many benchmark claims are fragile' vs 'Conclusions ... may not transfer' (holds); 'exact bed-slope correction' vs 'reproduce the exact bed increment' (holds); 'exact global minimizer' and the pick's proof claim (hold). Stays clean.

claims.claim: This period is split between algorithmic linear algebra, discretization analysis, and numerical reliability.
claims.span: Neutral framing of the four cited papers.

claims.claim: A deterministic sparse solver reaches bit complexity ~O(mn log(kappa/epsilon)) by combining Dixon lifting on a perturbed system with modular inversion and rational reconstruction.
claims.span: We give a deterministic algorithm ... using O~(mn log(κ/ε)) bit operations for inputs with logarithmically many bits per entry ... we apply Dixon's lifting algorithm to the perturbed system (A+I/R)x=b ... its modular inverse is trivial ... Fast rational reconstruction then recovers the exact solution

claims.claim: Giving ~O(n^2) for sparse polynomially conditioned inputs.
claims.span: For sparse, polynomially conditioned systems with m=O~(n), this gives an O~(n^2) algorithm for any inverse-polynomial accuracy

claims.claim: Closing much of the finite-precision gap to idealized CG.
claims.span: largely closing a gap between the idealized performance of the conjugate gradient method in exact arithmetic and the running time achievable with finite-precision computation

claims.claim: Finite local averages of the geodesic ray transform give Lipschitz stability on fixed finite-dimensional spaces.
